facts.label: Version relationships and comparability
facts.text: - The three 10-Qs and the 10-K are separate periodic reports, not versions of one another; each stays an active source. The Q3 10-Q repeats the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as its comparative: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:2, "December 31, 2025"]. Where the same period appears in two sources the filing controls the shareholder letter. - Stock split: the five-for-one split took effect in May 2026 and later reports restate share data: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:9, "five-for-one forward stock split"]. The FY2025 10-K and the Q1 10-Q cover pages show pre-split counts: [10-K FY2025, page:2, "142,736,197 shares of Class A common stock outstanding"]; [10-Q Q1 2026, page:1, "143,257,677 shares of Class A common stock outstanding"], against [10-Q Q2 2026, page:1, "719,916,415 shares of Class A common stock outstanding"]. - Period mix: the Q3 10-Q gives three-month and nine-month columns; the Q1 and Q2 10-Qs and letters give discrete quarter columns, so discrete Q1 and Q2 2026 are located. A discrete Q4 2025 column is not printed and would need the FY2025 annual figures less the nine months to September 30, 2025, a derivation left to CP-1. - Non-GAAP: the Adjusted EBITDA definition adds back share-based compensation, loss on debt extinguishment and others and subtracts warrant revenue: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:76, "minus revenue related to our Warrants"]. It is a company definition, not a covenant definition.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: On the company's own measure, leverage is moderate and falling. Total debt including finance leases is 5,261 at September 30, 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,752, a ratio of 1.91x, and net of unrestricted cash of 3,049 the ratio is 0.80x. The ratio has fallen at each of the four balance sheet dates read (FY2025 2.29x, Q1 2026 2.14x, Q2 2026 2.03x, Q3 2026 1.91x), driven by LTM EBITDA growth from 2,237 to 2,752 on debt that moved little. The headline understates three features. First, 1,125 of the debt is secured asset-based financing (floor plan, financing of retained securitization interests, sale-leaseback real estate financing and fleet financing), which is not corporate funded debt; the senior notes, term loan and unsecured notes total 4,036 (1.47x). Second, Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure that includes loan sale gains (1,084 in nine months 2026, 48.4% of the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,241) and adds back share-based compensation, while operating cash flow for those nine months was 900. Third, claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations: the tax receivable agreement liability (2,230), operating leases (469), and trade floor plan payables (300) that sit in accounts payable.

facts.label: Credit analysis
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: total debt including finance leases over LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.29x to 1.91x across four dates, while net debt fell from 2,806 to 2,212 as cash rose. Mechanism: EBITDA growth outpaced a flat debt stock, and the refinancing was debt neutral (1,660 in, 1,660 out) with a premium of 50 paid from cash. Implication: leverage is moderate on the company measure; of the debt, 1,125 is asset-based, so the measure mixes funding of inventory, receivables and property with corporate debt. Excluding asset-based debt, corporate funded debt is 4,036 (1.47x). Including trade floor plan payables (300) the ratio is 2.02x. - Coverage. Evidence: cash interest rose to 443 in nine months from 311 while interest expense, net fell to 298 from 407. Mechanism: the secured notes moved from payment-in-kind to cash coupons during 2025, so reported expense fell while cash paid rose; the refinancing then reduced the stated coupon on 1,660. Implication: cash cover of 5.88x is the right measure; it is the lowest of the four dates, so cover did not improve with leverage. Comparisons across the refinancing are not like for like. - Cash flow quality. Evidence: nine months operating cash flow 900 against Adjusted EBITDA 2,241; vehicle inventory used 1,025 and accounts payable and accrued liabilities provided 475. Mechanism: growth consumes working capital, and Adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash gain on loan sales (1,084) whose cash arrives through receivable sales in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was 734 in nine months 2026 (900 less 166), well below EBITDA; the credit depends on continued access to receivable sale and financing markets. - Liquidity. Evidence: cash 3,049 and availability 2,071; maturities cluster within twelve months. Mechanism: revolvers are borrowing-base limited and renewed routinely, and the receivable sale arrangements are committed with terms into 2027 and early 2028. Implication: day-to-day liquidity is adequate; a market disruption that cuts renewals or sale capacity would hit the 5,600 revolving lines and the sale capacity together. - Data quality and definition risks. Evidence: the redemption description differs between two sections of the Q3 report (see conflict below); the maturity table is stale; LTM figures are derived. Implication: figures that depend on these are labelled and carry the limitations in ## Gaps.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Carvana Co. is a holding company whose operating business sits in Carvana Group, LLC, a vertically integrated online retailer of used vehicles: it buys cars from consumers and wholesalers, reconditions them in owned sites, sells and delivers them nationally, finances customers, and sells the loans it originates. Management calls itself the leading platform in its market, which is Management Language; the filings document the model but not the ranking. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. Revenue is anchored on retail units, and every other stream (wholesale, loan sale gains, complementary products) is created by a retail sale, so volume, used-vehicle pricing and consumer credit availability move together. Profit depends heavily on selling loans into committed and market channels at a gain; that links earnings to the appetite of a few buyers and to benchmark rates, and management says it chose to give back margin to customers through lower loan rates. Funding is layered: corporate secured and unsecured debt at the holding company, plus asset-backed lines at operating and special purpose subsidiaries, as set out in the CP-1 handoff.

The only transaction in the latest quarter is the August 2026 refinancing, which left the debt amount unchanged and moved cost, maturity and rate profile. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The only new debt issue in the latest quarter is the term loan. On August 14, 2026, Carvana Co. entered into a credit agreement for a senior secured term loan B, fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75% of principal [10-Q Q3 2026, page:26, "which was fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%"]. The agreement is listed with the lenders and Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Barclays Bank PLC, as Administrative Agent and Syndication Agent"]. Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the proceeds redeemed in full the 2030 Senior Secured Notes [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "to redeem in full its 2030 Senior Secured Notes"]. Status: closed and drawn at the balance sheet date; the redemption is complete and treated as an extinguishment with a loss recognised in the quarter. Debt raised and retired are equal in principal (the amounts are in the CP-1 handoff); the premium paid on redemption came from cash, so the liquidity effect is a cash outflow equal to that premium with no change in debt. The CP-1 handoff logs a conflict on the accrued interest component of the redemption payment (1 in Note 9 against 4 in the management discussion); it is carried here as logged and not reconciled.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Terms that matter to creditors: the term loan is floating (Term SOFR plus a margin), amortizes 1.00% a year from March 2027, matures in 2033, ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes on the same first-priority collateral, and has no financial maintenance covenant [10-Q Q3 2026, page:27, "ranking pari passu with the Company's outstanding Senior Secured Notes"]. An interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028, so rate exposure returns for the remaining life [10-Q Q3 2026, page:52, "terminates on July 31, 2028"]. Prepayments through February 14, 2027 in connection with certain repricing transactions carry a 1.00% premium. The effect on the secured group is that the new lenders share the collateral equally with the remaining noteholders; the pro rata share of each depends on the principal amounts in the CP-1 handoff, and no intercreditor agreement is supplied. The preferred unit mechanism mirrors the debt: for each note retired one preferred unit of Carvana Group is retired, and one is issued for the term loan [10-Q Q3 2026, page:33, "issued 1.66 million of Class A Non-Convertible Preferred Units in conjunction with the incurrence of the Term Loan B"].

The effect on the secured group is that the new lenders share the collateral equally with the remaining noteholders; the pro rata share of each depends on the principal amounts in the CP-1 handoff, and no intercreditor agreement is supplied. The preferred unit mechanism mirrors the debt: for each note retired one preferred unit of Carvana Group is retired, and one is issued for the term loan [10-Q Q3 2026, page:33, "issued 1.66 million of Class A Non-Convertible Preferred Units in conjunction with the incurrence of the Term Loan B"].

facts.text: Earlier new financings in the evidence window: a fleet financing agreement with Citizens Bank in October 2025, a trade floor plan line with Stellantis Financial Services tied to franchise dealership purchases, and a seventh finance receivable facility in May 2026. Sale-capacity amendments with Ally (to a larger commitment through July 2027) and a loan purchase agreement upsize are receivable sales, not debt. No financial sponsor is involved, and no equity was raised through the at-the-market program in 2026; it had no activity in the first nine months [10-Q Q3 2026, page:32, "There was no activity pursuant to the ATM Program during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026."]. Subsequent to the quarter, the third finance receivable lender's maturity was extended to October 15, 2027; this is a subsequent event and is not folded into the September 30 facts.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: all four revenue lines flow from retail units, which grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 [10-Q Q3 2026, page:58, "increased by 39.4% to 217,385"]. Mechanism: growth has been volume-led while unit gross profit declined; durability depends on consumer demand, used-car prices and funding availability. Implication: revenue is strong but not contracted; a downturn would hit volume and gain-on-sale together. Conflicts that counter it: none logged. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: lower gross profit per unit and rising fuel and wage costs (cited above). Mechanism: management chose lower customer loan rates, which can reverse, but benchmark-rate and fuel moves are outside control. Implication: margin is sensitive to rates; cash conversion is lower than EBITDA suggests (CP-1 handoff). - Concentration risk. Evidence: Ally lends on the floor plan and buys loans; DriveTime administers product contracts. Mechanism: failure or renegotiation by either would hit funding or revenue. Implication: counterparty dependence is a monitoring item; shares are in ## Calculations. - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: Garcia Parties equity support in 2023, company equity issuance in 2025, no dividends. Mechanism: controlling holders have injected equity and kept cash in the business. Implication: alignment is supportive on the record, but the record is short and the controlling group can influence debt incurrence and distributions through its votes. - Key uncertainties: the 2023 exchange terms, the terms of the tax receivable agreement and related-party contracts, covenant levels, and the guarantor perimeter.

rows.label: Carvana is an online used-car retailer that sells, finances and delivers vehicles itself, growing fast on scale and loan sales. A controlling family, related-party dealings and a debt-neutral August refinancing frame creditor risk.
Revenue rests on retail units, with loan sale gains and product commissions riding on each unit.
The Garcia Parties hold most of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares.
DriveTime, a related party, administers vehicle service contracts and warranties, and Ally both lends and buys loans.
Documented behaviour since 2023 shows equity support and refinancing, with no dividend or debt-funded distribution found.
August 2026 refinancing swapped 9% secured notes for a floating-rate term loan, partly hedged.
Cause of lower unit gross profit
Shares outstanding at the latest practicable date

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Carvana has a sound but market-dependent fundamental credit profile: its debt is moderate against earnings, but those earnings depend on consumers, loan buyers and funding lines that can tighten together. The strongest support is financial. Total debt including finance leases of USD 5,261 million is 1.91x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and unrestricted cash of USD 3,049 million brings net leverage to 0.80x. The weakest point is quality and structure. Adjusted EBITDA includes loan sale gains equal to 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, operating cash flow trails EBITDA, and the control and related-party dealings of the Garcia Parties cannot be tested because the governing documents are not supplied. Continued access to loan sales and renewal of revolvers decide the outcome.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Moderate and improving leverage on a company-defined measure (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage chart table and Calculations). Carvana's total debt including finance leases was USD 5,261 million at Q3 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, a ratio of 1.91x, down from 2.29x at FY2025; net of USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash the ratio is 0.80x. The mechanism is EBITDA growth on a flat debt stock, so the improvement reflects earnings rather than repayment. Of the debt, USD 1,125 million is asset-based financing; corporate funded debt of USD 4,036 million is 1.47x. Including trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million the ratio is 2.02x. 2. Earnings quality is the central financial weakness (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis on cash flow quality and CP-1A Calculations). Loan sale gains of USD 1,084 million were 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,241 million, while operating cash flow was USD 900 million, 40.2% of that EBITDA, and free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was USD 734 million. The mechanism is that gains are recognised when loans are sold and the cash arrives through sale proceeds, with growth absorbing working capital. A pull-back by loan buyers would cut gain on sale and cash conversion at the same time. 3. Cash interest cover is adequate but did not improve with leverage (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 interest cover chart table). Cover was 5.88x at Q3 2026, the lowest of four dates, because cash interest paid rose as former payment-in-kind coupons turned to cash, even though interest expense, net fell. The August 2026 refinancing lowers the stated coupon, but the interest hedge ends on July 31, 2028 while the term loan runs to 2033. 4. Liquidity is strong on cash and conditional on collateral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity chart table and liquidity by facility). Carvana held USD 3,049 million of cash and USD 2,071 million of borrowing-base availability against USD 5,600 million of revolving commitments, of which USD 71 million was drawn; commitments of USD 3,900 million mature within twelve months after the October 2026 extension. The mechanism is renewal risk on lines that fund inventory and receivables; a market shock that cuts renewals and loan-sale capacity together would hit both sources. 5. Control and related-party dependence cannot be tested (Documentary Fact for the facts, Insufficient Information for capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership, governance and operating model rows). The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, and DriveTime, which they own, administers service contracts and warranties; its commissions are 21.2% of other sales and revenues and 8.4% of gross profit for the nine months. Ally, which lends on the floor plan, bought about 41.0% of the principal of loans sold. The documented record since 2023 is supportive (equity purchase, equity-funded note redemption, no dividends), but the agreements that would limit extraction or priming are not in the pack. 6. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure). The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,230 million, operating lease liabilities USD 469 million, and trade floor plan payables USD 300 million, equal to the size of that line. None is in the leverage ratio. 7. The term loan refinancing was debt neutral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Latest quarter and CP-1A Transaction summary). A USD 1,660 million term loan priced at Term SOFR plus 2.25% replaced USD 1,660 million of 9% secured notes, moving the maturity to 2033 and ranking pari passu with the 2031 secured notes. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, so headroom is not measurable.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Carvana has scale and momentum: retail units rose 39.4% in Q3 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 800 million in the quarter (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A operating model row on volume and CP-1 financial table). Management describes the platform as the leading one in its market, which is Management Language and is not adopted. Carvana has liquidity depth, with USD 3,049 million of cash and a broad set of revolving and loan-sale lines (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity tables and CP-1A loan sale model row). Its leverage has fallen at each of four balance sheet dates and its term-out of the 2030 secured notes removed the largest near-dated bullet shown in the printed schedule (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage and maturities chart tables). The documented conduct of the controlling holders since 2023 is supportive: equity support, equity-funded redemption and no dividends (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1A governance and sponsor behaviour table).

Unit economics are thinner: total gross profit per unit fell to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 from USD 7,362, and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% on an LTM basis against 11.0% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A unit economics row and CP-1 financial table). Management attributes the decline to giving back lower loan rates, which is Management Language. Carvana's funding is short-dated and collateral-limited, with counterparty concentration in Ally and DriveTime (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity by facility and CP-1A Calculations). Control by one group, related-party dealings and a tax receivable liability to related parties are not constrained by any document in the pack (Insufficient Information on capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership and governance rows). Covenant levels, guarantor schedules and a post-refinancing maturity schedule are missing, so protection and refinancing risk cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; basis: CP-0 and CP-1 gaps).

The Garcia Parties control about 83% of the voting power and related party DriveTime supplies services behind product revenue.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: CARVANA CO. (issuer id cvna, ticker CVNA, Delaware registrant, Commission File Number 001-38073). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot, case kind public. Reporting currency: USD, with the filings stating amounts in millions unless a locator says otherwise. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026). Prior period: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025).

Question answered by this module: can the effective source set support the requested downstream work (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5), and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. It separates source sufficiency from completion of downstream analysis. The context file carries no deal terms, quotes, ratings, valuation inputs, peers, attachments or research questions (its legal-documents attachment flag is "none"); those blanks are treated as not supplied, not as zero.
Citation form used below: [source label, page:N, "exact substring"]. A page is the source chunk shown as page:N, not a printed page number. Source labels are defined in `## Sources`.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

The context holds the user's dated settings (run type, pathway, as-of date, cutoff, current and prior period, reporting currency, identity). It is not issuer evidence.
### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module of this run and CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff.
### Not relied on
The pack also holds a retrieval log named _retrieval.json, which the launcher ignored. It was not used as evidence.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filed reports and shareholder letters are sufficient for the financial snapshot, with named limits. All four downstream consumers can run, each with limitations. | Medium | No executed financing documents, no updated maturity schedule after the August refinancing, and no ratings or market inputs are in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Seven issuer sources cover the latest annual report, three quarterly reports and three shareholder letters, all dated before the cutoff. | Statements, debt notes, liquidity tables and non-GAAP reconciliations can be read for the current and prior period. | High |

| Financing terms come from filing descriptions only, not from the indentures or credit agreements. | Basket capacity, covenant definitions and lien terms stay unverified until the documents are supplied. | High |
| The latest principal maturity table predates the term loan refinancing. | The maturity wall must be rebuilt from instrument terms, with that limitation carried forward. | High |
| A five-for-one stock split changes share data comparability across the sources. | Per-share and share-count figures need a split label before any cross-period use. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested snapshot work with limitations. Every consumer is assessed READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS: the owner of each workflow can perform its method on the located evidence, and no consumer is conditional on a missing source or blocked by unusable evidence. This is a statement about source sufficiency only; it is not a statement that downstream analysis is complete, and no normalized quarter, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance is asserted (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED). The evidence is filed financial statements and notes (audited for FY2025, unaudited for the 2026 quarters) plus unaudited management shareholder letters. The strongest contrary evidence is the absence of any executed legal or financing document, so every governing term below rests on the issuer's own description of it.
### Source register
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Located coverage and status |

| 10-K FY2025 | Annual report on Form 10-K; filed statements with an audit opinion; controls the facts it states | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries, consolidated | Year ended December 31, 2025, with comparatives; reporting unit is a single segment | Statements, debt note with principal maturities, liquidity table, leases, tax receivable agreement, related parties, litigation, exhibit list; text extracted from all pages, no fidelity review |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q; unaudited filed statements | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three months ended March 31, 2026, versus the prior-year quarter and December 31, 2025 balances | Statements, debt note, liquidity table, non-GAAP reconciliation, supplemental cash flow; cash flow is year-to-date only |

| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q; unaudited filed statements | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three and six months ended June 30, 2026 | Same profile; first filing to carry the stock split; includes a subsequent-events note on the Ally amendment |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q; unaudited filed statements; current-period anchor | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 | Same profile plus the August term loan and bond redemption, the interest rate swap, the Root warrant exchange, the Ally amendment and the exhibit list |

| EX-99.1 Q1 2026 | Earnings release and shareholder letter; management attributed claims, unaudited | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries | Q1 2026 | Narrative, statements, liquidity table, non-GAAP reconciliation; no presentation deck in the pack |
| EX-99.1 Q2 2026 | Earnings release and shareholder letter; management attributed claims, unaudited | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries | Q2 2026 and first half 2026 | Same profile |

| EX-99.1 Q3 2026 | Earnings release and shareholder letter; management attributed claims, unaudited | Carvana Co. and subsidiaries | Q3 2026 and trailing quarters | Same profile plus outlook, a note on 2027 reporting, a quarterly trend table and a liquidity table |

Cover evidence for identity and period: [10-K FY2025, page:1, "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025"]; [10-Q Q1 2026, page:1, "For the Quarterly Period Ended March 31, 2026"]; [10-Q Q2 2026, page:1, "For the Quarterly Period Ended June 30, 2026"]; [10-Q Q3 2026, page:1, "For the Quarterly Period Ended September 30, 2026"]. The filing dates are in the pack's retrieval log, not in the extracted text: the latest filing is the Q3 report and its signature page is dated [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Date: October 28, 2026"], before the cutoff. No source in the pack is dated after the cutoff.

Authority and extraction fidelity are separate. The FY2025 statements carry an auditor opinion: [10-K FY2025, page:96, "present fairly, in all material respects"]. The quarterly statements are unaudited: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:2, "Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets"]. The shareholder letters are management communications; where a letter and a filing differ, the filing controls. Extraction here is visible text per chunk; successful extraction is not a fidelity review, and no table was checked against an image.
### Entity roles and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Carvana Co., the registrant, consolidates Carvana Group, LLC as a variable interest entity of which it is the primary beneficiary: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:8, "Carvana Co. owned approximately 65.1% of Carvana Group"]. Non-controlling interests are therefore part of the consolidated equity: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:3, "Non-controlling interests 1,301 762"].

- Borrower and issuer roles: the term loan credit agreement is listed with Carvana Co. as a party and Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Credit Agreement, dated as of August 14, 2026, among Carvana Co., the lenders party thereto and Barclays Bank PLC, as Administrative Agent and Syndication Agent"].

- Guarantors: the senior secured notes are guaranteed by the domestic restricted subsidiaries with listed exceptions: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior secured basis, jointly and severally, by all of the domestic restricted subsidiaries"]. The pack contains no guarantor schedule naming the individual guarantors. The unsecured notes are described only as guaranteed by "certain" subsidiaries: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:28, "are guaranteed by certain of the Company's subsidiaries"].

- Unrestricted perimeter: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:28, "designated ADESA and its subsidiaries as unrestricted subsidiaries"] under the unsecured note indentures. The treatment of ADESA under the secured note indentures and the term loan is not stated in the located text.

- Special-purpose perimeter: the receivable financing subsidiaries are wholly owned special purpose entities whose assets are not available to the general creditors: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:24, "whose assets are not available to the general creditors of the Company"]. Scope of this module: the financial base for the credit snapshot. It reports the financial statements by period, the debt of the issuer instrument by instrument, liquidity by facility, covenants, maturities, claims outside the debt figure, the Adjusted EBITDA definition, the latest quarter and subsequent events, and four chart tables. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage on Adjusted EBITDA fell each period from 2.29x at FY2025 to 1.91x at Q3 2026 and cash rose to 3,049. Interest cover stayed above 5x, but Adjusted EBITDA is a company definition. | Medium | Financing documents and covenant levels are not in the pack, so protections and headroom cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt including finance leases was 5,261 at Q3 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,752, a ratio of 1.91x. | Moderate leverage on the company measure, but 1,125 of the debt is secured asset financing. | Medium |

| The August 2026 refinancing replaced 1,660 of 9% secured notes with a term loan priced at Term SOFR plus 2.25%, with a partial interest hedge. | Lower coupon cost, but floating-rate exposure beyond mid-2028 and a later maturity wall. | High |
| Of 5,600 revolving commitments, 2,071 was available to borrow at Q3 2026, and most commitments mature within twelve months. | Liquidity depends on collateral and on routine renewals. | High |
| Adjusted EBITDA includes loan sale gains of 1,084 in the nine months to Q3 2026, and operating cash flow was 900. | Cash conversion is lower than the EBITDA figure suggests. | Medium |
| A tax receivable agreement liability of 2,230 and trade floor plan payables of 300 sit outside the reported debt. | These claims add to fixed obligations beyond the debt ratio. | High |
### Financial base view

On the company's own measure, leverage is moderate and falling. Total debt including finance leases is 5,261 at September 30, 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,752, a ratio of 1.91x, and net of unrestricted cash of 3,049 the ratio is 0.80x. The ratio has fallen at each of the four balance sheet dates read (FY2025 2.29x, Q1 2026 2.14x, Q2 2026 2.03x, Q3 2026 1.91x), driven by LTM EBITDA growth from 2,237 to 2,752 on debt that moved little. The headline understates three features. First, 1,125 of the debt is secured asset-based financing (floor plan, financing of retained securitization interests, sale-leaseback real estate financing and fleet financing), which is not corporate funded debt; the senior notes, term loan and unsecured notes total 4,036 (1.47x). Second, Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined measure that includes loan sale gains (1,084 in nine months 2026, 48.4% of the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,241) and adds back share-based compensation, while operating cash flow for those nine months was 900. Third, claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations: the tax receivable agreement liability (2,230), operating leases (469), and trade floor plan payables (300) that sit in accounts payable.

Interest cover on cash interest is above 5x at every date but is lowest at Q3 2026 (5.88x), because cash interest paid in the nine months rose to 443 from 311 as the former payment-in-kind coupons turned to cash, even though interest expense, net fell to 298 from 407. The August 2026 refinancing (a 1,660 term loan at Term SOFR plus 2.25%, replacing 1,660 of 9% notes) lowers the stated coupon, but the interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028 and the term loan matures in 2033.

Liquidity is strong on cash (3,049) but the borrowing capacity is collateral-limited: revolving commitments are 5,600 and outstanding 71, yet availability under the borrowing base is 2,071. Most commitments mature within twelve months of the balance sheet date. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, and compliance with all debt covenants is stated; covenant levels and headroom for the other facilities are Not supplied. The view is a base for the credit snapshot, not a credit conclusion; the four limits above and the gaps in `## Gaps` apply to every use of it.

### Credit analysis

- Leverage. Evidence: total debt including finance leases over LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.29x to 1.91x across four dates, while net debt fell from 2,806 to 2,212 as cash rose. Mechanism: EBITDA growth outpaced a flat debt stock, and the refinancing was debt neutral (1,660 in, 1,660 out) with a premium of 50 paid from cash. Implication: leverage is moderate on the company measure; of the debt, 1,125 is asset-based, so the measure mixes funding of inventory, receivables and property with corporate debt. Excluding asset-based debt, corporate funded debt is 4,036 (1.47x). Including trade floor plan payables (300) the ratio is 2.02x.

- Coverage. Evidence: cash interest rose to 443 in nine months from 311 while interest expense, net fell to 298 from 407. Mechanism: the secured notes moved from payment-in-kind to cash coupons during 2025, so reported expense fell while cash paid rose; the refinancing then reduced the stated coupon on 1,660. Implication: cash cover of 5.88x is the right measure; it is the lowest of the four dates, so cover did not improve with leverage. Comparisons across the refinancing are not like for like.

- Cash flow quality. Evidence: nine months operating cash flow 900 against Adjusted EBITDA 2,241; vehicle inventory used 1,025 and accounts payable and accrued liabilities provided 475. Mechanism: growth consumes working capital, and Adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash gain on loan sales (1,084) whose cash arrives through receivable sales in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was 734 in nine months 2026 (900 less 166), well below EBITDA; the credit depends on continued access to receivable sale and financing markets.

- Liquidity. Evidence: cash 3,049 and availability 2,071; maturities cluster within twelve months. Mechanism: revolvers are borrowing-base limited and renewed routinely, and the receivable sale arrangements are committed with terms into 2027 and early 2028. Implication: day-to-day liquidity is adequate; a market disruption that cuts renewals or sale capacity would hit the 5,600 revolving lines and the sale capacity together.

- Data quality and definition risks. Evidence: the redemption description differs between two sections of the Q3 report (see conflict below); the maturity table is stale; LTM figures are derived. Implication: figures that depend on these are labelled and carry the limitations in `## Gaps`.

- Accrued interest on the August 2026 redemption: Note 9 states the 2030 Senior Secured Notes were redeemed for 1,711, which included 50 of premium and 1 of accrued interest: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "which included $50 million of premium and $1 million of accrued interest"]; the management discussion states 4 of accrued interest: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:74, "which included $50 million of premium and $4 million of accrued interest"]. Question answered: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of Carvana Co. Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. Scope limits: no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Financial figures are taken from the CP-1 handoff or from the quotes below; figures not in either are computed in `## Calculations`.

Category tags used on every fact row: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, qualified and never adopted), Analyst Interpretation (a reading of cited evidence), Insufficient Information (the evidence is missing; the missing datapoint is named). Citation form: [source label, page:N, "exact substring"]; a page is the source chunk page:N, not a printed page.
## Sources

Run settings source: context, sha256 3b0d728dae64d48f4491be2af6d53653b4803495916d71df1f3f2f764a94f8be. It supplies the sector label and shows no sponsor, deal terms or ratings; it is not issuer evidence.
### Supplied handoffs

### Evidence quality

Located filings and the audited FY2025 statements are primary, dated and issuer-specific (High). Shareholder letters are management communications (Medium for facts they restate from filings; Management Language otherwise). No external source is used; the sector label comes from the context. No transaction document, indenture, credit agreement, LLC agreement or tax receivable agreement is in the pack, so legal capacity is described only as the filings describe it.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Carvana is an online used-car retailer that sells, finances and delivers vehicles itself, growing fast on scale and loan sales. A controlling family, related-party dealings and a debt-neutral August refinancing frame creditor risk. | Medium | No financing, ownership or related-party agreements are in the pack, so control and capacity rest on filing descriptions. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Revenue rests on retail units, with loan sale gains and product commissions riding on each unit. | Earnings follow vehicle demand and the willingness of buyers to take loans; both can reverse together. | High |

| The Garcia Parties hold most of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares. | Control over debt incurrence and distributions sits with one group; documents limiting it are not supplied. | High |
| DriveTime, a related party, administers vehicle service contracts and warranties, and Ally both lends and buys loans. | Concentrated counterparties add dependency risk to the cash flow. | High |

| Documented behaviour since 2023 shows equity support and refinancing, with no dividend or debt-funded distribution found. | No extraction pattern found; the 2023 exchange terms are not in the pack. | Medium |
| August 2026 refinancing swapped 9% secured notes for a floating-rate term loan, partly hedged. | Lower stated cost, later maturity, rate exposure after the hedge ends. | High |
### Business and transaction view

Carvana Co. is a holding company whose operating business sits in Carvana Group, LLC, a vertically integrated online retailer of used vehicles: it buys cars from consumers and wholesalers, reconditions them in owned sites, sells and delivers them nationally, finances customers, and sells the loans it originates. Management calls itself the leading platform in its market, which is Management Language; the filings document the model but not the ranking. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. Revenue is anchored on retail units, and every other stream (wholesale, loan sale gains, complementary products) is created by a retail sale, so volume, used-vehicle pricing and consumer credit availability move together. Profit depends heavily on selling loans into committed and market channels at a gain; that links earnings to the appetite of a few buyers and to benchmark rates, and management says it chose to give back margin to customers through lower loan rates. Funding is layered: corporate secured and unsecured debt at the holding company, plus asset-backed lines at operating and special purpose subsidiaries, as set out in the CP-1 handoff.

Ownership and governance matter to creditors more than usual. The Garcia Parties control most of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares, the company is a controlled company, and DriveTime, owned by the same parties, supplies services on which revenue depends. The documented conduct since 2023 is mostly supportive (an equity purchase to fund a note tender, equity issuance to redeem secured notes, no dividends), but the agreements that limit what the controlling group could do are not in the pack, so capacity to act against creditors cannot be assessed. The only transaction in the latest quarter is the August 2026 refinancing, which left the debt amount unchanged and moved cost, maturity and rate profile. Subsequent to the quarter, one revolving facility was extended.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only new debt issue in the latest quarter is the term loan. On August 14, 2026, Carvana Co. entered into a credit agreement for a senior secured term loan B, fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75% of principal [10-Q Q3 2026, page:26, "which was fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%"]. The agreement is listed with the lenders and Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent [10-Q Q3 2026, page:88, "Barclays Bank PLC, as Administrative Agent and Syndication Agent"]. Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the proceeds redeemed in full the 2030 Senior Secured Notes [10-Q Q3 2026, page:25, "to redeem in full its 2030 Senior Secured Notes"]. Status: closed and drawn at the balance sheet date; the redemption is complete and treated as an extinguishment with a loss recognised in the quarter. Debt raised and retired are equal in principal (the amounts are in the CP-1 handoff); the premium paid on redemption came from cash, so the liquidity effect is a cash outflow equal to that premium with no change in debt. The CP-1 handoff logs a conflict on the accrued interest component of the redemption payment (1 in Note 9 against 4 in the management discussion); it is carried here as logged and not reconciled.

Terms that matter to creditors: the term loan is floating (Term SOFR plus a margin), amortizes 1.00% a year from March 2027, matures in 2033, ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes on the same first-priority collateral, and has no financial maintenance covenant [10-Q Q3 2026, page:27, "ranking pari passu with the Company's outstanding Senior Secured Notes"]. An interest rate swap hedges only to July 31, 2028, so rate exposure returns for the remaining life [10-Q Q3 2026, page:52, "terminates on July 31, 2028"]. Prepayments through February 14, 2027 in connection with certain repricing transactions carry a 1.00% premium. The effect on the secured group is that the new lenders share the collateral equally with the remaining noteholders; the pro rata share of each depends on the principal amounts in the CP-1 handoff, and no intercreditor agreement is supplied. The preferred unit mechanism mirrors the debt: for each note retired one preferred unit of Carvana Group is retired, and one is issued for the term loan [10-Q Q3 2026, page:33, "issued 1.66 million of Class A Non-Convertible Preferred Units in conjunction with the incurrence of the Term Loan B"].

Earlier new financings in the evidence window: a fleet financing agreement with Citizens Bank in October 2025, a trade floor plan line with Stellantis Financial Services tied to franchise dealership purchases, and a seventh finance receivable facility in May 2026. Sale-capacity amendments with Ally (to a larger commitment through July 2027) and a loan purchase agreement upsize are receivable sales, not debt. No financial sponsor is involved, and no equity was raised through the at-the-market program in 2026; it had no activity in the first nine months [10-Q Q3 2026, page:32, "There was no activity pursuant to the ATM Program during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026."]. Subsequent to the quarter, the third finance receivable lender's maturity was extended to October 15, 2027; this is a subsequent event and is not folded into the September 30 facts.

- Capacity: ADESA site conversion continues and is partly debt-financed (see above). Mechanism: capital intensity rises with units; part of it enters as asset-backed debt.
- Equity: the five-for-one split adjusts share counts, not ownership percentages; no buyback occurred in FY2025.

- Monitoring items the source set lacks: a post-refinancing debt and maturity schedule, covenant certificates for the secured notes and floor plan, a guarantor schedule, an Adjusted EBITDA bridge to a covenant definition (the company bridge to net income is supplied), and the executed financing, tax receivable and related-party agreements.

- Revenue durability. Evidence: all four revenue lines flow from retail units, which grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 [10-Q Q3 2026, page:58, "increased by 39.4% to 217,385"]. Mechanism: growth has been volume-led while unit gross profit declined; durability depends on consumer demand, used-car prices and funding availability. Implication: revenue is strong but not contracted; a downturn would hit volume and gain-on-sale together. Conflicts that counter it: none logged.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: lower gross profit per unit and rising fuel and wage costs (cited above). Mechanism: management chose lower customer loan rates, which can reverse, but benchmark-rate and fuel moves are outside control. Implication: margin is sensitive to rates; cash conversion is lower than EBITDA suggests (CP-1 handoff).

- Concentration risk. Evidence: Ally lends on the floor plan and buys loans; DriveTime administers product contracts. Mechanism: failure or renegotiation by either would hit funding or revenue. Implication: counterparty dependence is a monitoring item; shares are in `## Calculations`.

- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: Garcia Parties equity support in 2023, company equity issuance in 2025, no dividends. Mechanism: controlling holders have injected equity and kept cash in the business. Implication: alignment is supportive on the record, but the record is short and the controlling group can influence debt incurrence and distributions through its votes.

- Ally share of principal sold, nine months 2026: Ally 5.7 billion; securitizations 3.7 billion; fixed pool sales 4.5 billion; total 13.9 billion; Ally share 5.7 / 13.9 = 41.0%. The inputs are printed in rounded billions, so the share is approximate. Inputs: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:18, "the Company sold $2.0 billion and $1.2 billion, respectively, in principal balances of finance receivables under the Ally MPSA"], [10-Q Q3 2026, page:18, "$5.7 billion and $3.2 billion, respectively, in principal balances of finance receivables under the Ally MPSA"], [10-Q Q3 2026, page:18, "$3.7 billion and $2.6 billion, respectively, in principal balances of finance receivables through securitization transactions"], and [10-Q Q3 2026, page:19, "completed fixed pool loan sales of $4.5 billion"].

- Executed agreements (indentures, term loan credit agreement, floor plan, LLC agreement, tax receivable agreement, Ally and DriveTime agreements) are Not supplied: legal capacity of the controlling group and of the company under debt documents cannot be assessed (CP-0 gaps G1, G2, G4, G10 remain open).

- No presentation decks; slide-level content is not claimed (CP-0 gap G7). The shareholder letters are Management Language where they characterise performance.
- The trade floor plan line change from 214 to 300 is not explained in the sources.

This module gives the fundamental credit view of CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway, current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025, in USD. It synthesises the financial base and the business and transaction context supplied by the upstream handoffs, and it takes no new facts from the filings.
## Sources

The run settings source (context, sha256 3b0d728dae64d48f4491be2af6d53653b4803495916d71df1f3f2f764a94f8be) holds dated settings and no issuer evidence.
### Supplied handoffs

| CP-1A | a5ea306dff2d8225beff86753d4f17e13f65167966a1c42cb4f68ef5725ddd14 | Business and transaction context; READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for this module |

All figures below are those printed in the CP-1 handoff (Financials and credit metrics, the four chart tables and Calculations) or the CP-1A handoff (Calculations). Basis references in the tables name the handoff and the section.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Carvana has a sound but market-dependent credit profile: leverage is moderate at 1.91x and cash is large, but earnings rely on loan buyers, consumers and short-dated funding lines. | Medium | Debt documents, covenant levels and related-party agreements are not supplied, so protections and control cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt of USD 5,261 million is 1.91x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and net leverage is 0.80x. | Moderate leverage on the company measure, improving at each of four dates. | Medium |

| Loan sale gains equal 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow was USD 900 million against EBITDA of USD 2,241 million. | Earnings quality and cash conversion depend on loan buyers staying active. | Medium |

| Of USD 5,600 million of revolving commitments, USD 2,071 million was available, and USD 3,900 million of commitments mature within twelve months. | Liquidity is adequate but depends on borrowing-base collateral and routine renewals. | High |

| The Garcia Parties control about 83% of the voting power and related party DriveTime supplies services behind product revenue. | Control and dependence risk cannot be tested without the governing documents. | High |
| The tax receivable liability, operating leases and trade floor plan payables sit outside the debt ratio. | Fixed obligations are larger than the reported debt. | High |
### Credit view

Carvana has a sound but market-dependent fundamental credit profile: its debt is moderate against earnings, but those earnings depend on consumers, loan buyers and funding lines that can tighten together. The strongest support is financial. Total debt including finance leases of USD 5,261 million is 1.91x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and unrestricted cash of USD 3,049 million brings net leverage to 0.80x. The weakest point is quality and structure. Adjusted EBITDA includes loan sale gains equal to 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, operating cash flow trails EBITDA, and the control and related-party dealings of the Garcia Parties cannot be tested because the governing documents are not supplied. Continued access to loan sales and renewal of revolvers decide the outcome.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Sound but market-dependent: moderate leverage and strong cash, with earnings that rely on loan sale markets and short-dated asset-backed funding | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage and liquidity chart tables; CP-1A operating model rows on loan sales and unit economics |

| Thesis | Carvana can service its debt from growing, scaled earnings, provided loan buyers and revolving lenders keep supporting a model that sells most of what it originates | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Credit analysis (leverage, coverage, cash flow quality, liquidity); CP-1A Business and transaction view |
The confidence is below High because no executed financing document is available, the post-refinancing maturity schedule is not printed, and ratings are Not supplied (see `## Gaps`).
### Key findings

1. Moderate and improving leverage on a company-defined measure (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage chart table and Calculations). Carvana's total debt including finance leases was USD 5,261 million at Q3 2026 against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, a ratio of 1.91x, down from 2.29x at FY2025; net of USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash the ratio is 0.80x. The mechanism is EBITDA growth on a flat debt stock, so the improvement reflects earnings rather than repayment. Of the debt, USD 1,125 million is asset-based financing; corporate funded debt of USD 4,036 million is 1.47x. Including trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million the ratio is 2.02x.

2. Earnings quality is the central financial weakness (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis on cash flow quality and CP-1A Calculations). Loan sale gains of USD 1,084 million were 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,241 million, while operating cash flow was USD 900 million, 40.2% of that EBITDA, and free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment was USD 734 million. The mechanism is that gains are recognised when loans are sold and the cash arrives through sale proceeds, with growth absorbing working capital. A pull-back by loan buyers would cut gain on sale and cash conversion at the same time.

3. Cash interest cover is adequate but did not improve with leverage (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 interest cover chart table). Cover was 5.88x at Q3 2026, the lowest of four dates, because cash interest paid rose as former payment-in-kind coupons turned to cash, even though interest expense, net fell. The August 2026 refinancing lowers the stated coupon, but the interest hedge ends on July 31, 2028 while the term loan runs to 2033.

4. Liquidity is strong on cash and conditional on collateral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity chart table and liquidity by facility). Carvana held USD 3,049 million of cash and USD 2,071 million of borrowing-base availability against USD 5,600 million of revolving commitments, of which USD 71 million was drawn; commitments of USD 3,900 million mature within twelve months after the October 2026 extension. The mechanism is renewal risk on lines that fund inventory and receivables; a market shock that cuts renewals and loan-sale capacity together would hit both sources.

5. Control and related-party dependence cannot be tested (Documentary Fact for the facts, Insufficient Information for capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership, governance and operating model rows). The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, and DriveTime, which they own, administers service contracts and warranties; its commissions are 21.2% of other sales and revenues and 8.4% of gross profit for the nine months. Ally, which lends on the floor plan, bought about 41.0% of the principal of loans sold. The documented record since 2023 is supportive (equity purchase, equity-funded note redemption, no dividends), but the agreements that would limit extraction or priming are not in the pack.

6. Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed obligations (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure). The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,230 million, operating lease liabilities USD 469 million, and trade floor plan payables USD 300 million, equal to the size of that line. None is in the leverage ratio.

7. The term loan refinancing was debt neutral (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 Latest quarter and CP-1A Transaction summary). A USD 1,660 million term loan priced at Term SOFR plus 2.25% replaced USD 1,660 million of 9% secured notes, moving the maturity to 2033 and ranking pari passu with the 2031 secured notes. No financial maintenance covenant applies to the term loan, so headroom is not measurable.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Carvana has scale and momentum: retail units rose 39.4% in Q3 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 800 million in the quarter (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A operating model row on volume and CP-1 financial table). Management describes the platform as the leading one in its market, which is Management Language and is not adopted. Carvana has liquidity depth, with USD 3,049 million of cash and a broad set of revolving and loan-sale lines (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity tables and CP-1A loan sale model row). Its leverage has fallen at each of four balance sheet dates and its term-out of the 2030 secured notes removed the largest near-dated bullet shown in the printed schedule (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 leverage and maturities chart tables). The documented conduct of the controlling holders since 2023 is supportive: equity support, equity-funded redemption and no dividends (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1A governance and sponsor behaviour table).

Weaknesses. Carvana's earnings depend on gain on sale: loan sale gains are 48.4% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, and other revenue carries no cost of sales, so margin follows funding markets (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Credit analysis and CP-1A operating model rows). Unit economics are thinner: total gross profit per unit fell to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 from USD 7,362, and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% on an LTM basis against 11.0% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1A unit economics row and CP-1 financial table). Management attributes the decline to giving back lower loan rates, which is Management Language. Carvana's funding is short-dated and collateral-limited, with counterparty concentration in Ally and DriveTime (Documentary Fact; basis: CP-1 liquidity by facility and CP-1A Calculations). Control by one group, related-party dealings and a tax receivable liability to related parties are not constrained by any document in the pack (Insufficient Information on capacity; basis: CP-1A ownership and governance rows). Covenant levels, guarantor schedules and a post-refinancing maturity schedule are missing, so protection and refinancing risk cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; basis: CP-0 and CP-1 gaps).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Loan sale market dependence | Gains and cash arrive when loans are sold to a few buyers; buyers and spreads can change together with consumer credit conditions | Lower EBITDA and weaker cash conversion with the retained interests and warranty exposure remaining | Material | CP-1A loan sale model and concentration rows; CP-1 cash flow quality |

| Short-dated, collateral-limited revolvers | Most commitments mature within twelve months and availability follows eligible inventory and receivables | Liquidity can shrink in a downturn when collateral values and renewals both weaken | Material | CP-1 liquidity by facility |

| Margin sensitivity to rates and fuel | Management chose lower customer loan rates and fuel and wages are rising | Lower unit economics lower coverage and delay deleveraging | Material | CP-1A unit economics and cost rows |

| Control and unverified protections | One group directs debt incurrence and distributions; baskets and covenants are not supplied | Priming, leakage or extraction cannot be excluded or measured | Material | CP-1A ownership and governance rows |

| Refinancing and rate exposure after the hedge | The swap ends July 31, 2028 while the term loan runs to 2033 | Higher floating cost in the later years and a bunched secured stack | Material | CP-1 instrument table and Latest quarter |

| Claims outside the debt figure | Tax receivable payments, leases and trade floor plan payables are cash calls ahead of equity but outside leverage | Fixed charges exceed what the ratio shows | Minor | CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure |

| Documentation gaps | Executed agreements, ratings and the 2023 exchange terms are missing | Protections, recoveries mechanics and creditor-adverse history cannot be assessed | Material | CP-0 gaps and CP-1A gaps |

Recovery prospects appear only as a mechanic: the asset-backed lines and secured notes carry collateral, and the unsecured notes and other claims do not; no expected recovery outcome is stated. No peer ranking or instrument recommendation is made; relative value belongs to a later module.
### Consistency with the upstream handoffs

The CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs agree on the figures used here. The logged accrued-interest conflict on the 2026 redemption (1 in the debt note against 4 in the management discussion) is carried unresolved; it does not enter any figure in this view. CP-1 updated the CP-0 guarantor point (ADESA excluded for the unsecured notes only); this module follows CP-1.
## Calculations

No new calculation is made. Every figure above is taken from the CP-1 handoff (Financial base view, chart tables, Financials and credit metrics, Calculations) or the CP-1A handoff (Calculations: DriveTime commissions 21.2% of other sales and revenues and 8.4% of gross profit; Ally 41.0% of principal sold, approximate because the inputs are in rounded billions).
## Gaps

- Executed indentures, the term loan credit agreement, the floor plan agreement, the LLC agreement, the tax receivable agreement and the related-party agreements are Not supplied. Control, baskets, lien priority and the cost of leakage cannot be tested. The 1,500 and 750 debt baskets in the liquidity table are issuer statements (Severity: high).
- No post-refinancing principal maturity schedule: the printed schedule is as of December 31, 2025 and includes the redeemed 2030 notes. The maturity wall is a derived view (Severity: medium).
- Covenant levels and headroom for the secured notes, unsecured notes and floor plan facility are Not supplied; compliance is asserted only (Severity: medium).
- Ratings, market data and valuation inputs are Not supplied (Severity: medium for later modules, none for this one).
- The 2023 exchange terms are not in the pack, so creditor-adverse behaviour in 2023 is Insufficient Information (Severity: medium).
- Adjusted EBITDA is a company definition; the figures are LTM derived by subtraction. Share counts are not used. The accrued-interest conflict is unresolved.
- Readiness: CP-1A recorded READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for this module and no blocked module feeds it, so confidence is capped at Medium by the gaps above.
## Next module

CP-5 should trace each figure in this view back to the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs and to the sources they cite, check that the category tags match the evidence, and carry the open gaps and the logged conflict.

### Evidence trace view

The analysis of Carvana is traceable enough for a restricted committee use but not for a clean one. The strongest support is mechanical: every cited quote was found verbatim on its cited page, the derived figures recomputed exactly, and the CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2 figures agree with one another. The weakest point is evidential: the maturity chart still shows the schedule printed before the August 2026 refinancing, including the 2030 Senior Secured Notes that were redeemed, and legal structure, guarantor perimeter, debt baskets and control limits are described only as the issuer describes them because no executed document is in the pack. Two issues are Material and five are Minor, with none Critical. Supplying the financing documents and rebuilding the maturity chart would lift the restriction.

### Clearance decision
CLEARANCE DECISION: Pass with Remediation. Critical Issues: 0. Material Issues: 2. Minor Issues: 5. Committee Use: Restricted.

The figures and quotes are sound, but the maturity chart is stale (I-01) and the legal and control claims lack executed documents (I-02), so committee use is restricted until those are disclosed or fixed. The Material issues must be disclosed with any committee use of the leverage, maturity or protection conclusions. committee_status: Restricted; qa_status: Restricted. No numeric confidence score is stated because the scoring script is not available in this run.
### Independent checks performed

1. Locators: all 248 bracket citations in the three source-citing handoffs (48 in CP-0, 119 in CP-1, 81 in CP-1A) were re-run as exact-substring searches on the cited page of the cited source; none failed. CP-2 cites no source text by design and relies on the other handoffs.
2. Claim support: for each material claim the cited quote was read for whether it states the claim, not just whether it exists. Weak cases are listed in the appendix (I-04).
3. Recalculation: every derived figure used in CP-2 was recomputed from the cited inputs; results are in `## Calculations`.
4. Identity: each figure repeated in CP-2 was compared with the same figure in CP-1 or CP-1A for value, unit, period and perimeter. All matched except for missing period or date labels (I-03).

5. Perimeter: the debt, EBITDA and cash figures are for Carvana Co. and subsidiaries consolidated. Carvana is a retailer rather than a finance company, but 1,125 of asset-based financing (floor plan, financing of retained securitization interests, real estate and fleet financing) is separated from corporate funded debt of 4,036 in CP-1 and used that way in CP-2.
6. Subsequent events: the October 2026 extension of one receivable facility is flagged as a subsequent event in CP-1 and CP-1A and is not blended into September 30 facts.

All inputs are quoted figures from the cited handoffs or sources, in US$ millions.

- Balance sheet carrying basis for debt (short-term revolving facilities plus current portion plus long-term debt): December 31, 2025, 58 + 227 + 4,830 = 5,115; September 30, 2026, 71 + 283 + 4,874 = 5,228. Inputs: [10-Q Q3 2026, page:2, "Short-term revolving facilities 71 58"]; [10-Q Q3 2026, page:2, "Current portion of long-term debt 283 227"]; [10-Q Q3 2026, page:2, "Long-term debt, excluding current portion 4,874 4,830"].
- Gross delta to the principal basis used in CP-1: 5,133 - 5,115 = 18 at December 31, 2025 and 5,261 - 5,228 = 33 at September 30, 2026.

- Leverage on the carrying basis: December 31, 2025, 5,115 / 2,237 = 2.29x and net (5,115 - 2,327) / 2,237 = 1.25x; September 30, 2026, 5,228 / 2,752 = 1.90x and net (5,228 - 3,049) / 2,752 = 0.79x. These agree with CP-1 within 0.01x (1.91x and 0.80x), so the basis does not change any conclusion.
